data.narrative:
Precision Neuroscience, a Series C biotech company founded by Benjamin Rapoport, Michael Mager, Demetrios Papageorgiou, and Mark Hettick, has raised $180M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 3 same-stage, same-sector private comparables in Biotech & Health, supplemented by 3 public sector anchors (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $180M total raised proxy, yielding $306M. Peer-median anchoring references 3 Series C biotech peers—Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B)—generating a median valuation of $3.8B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied due to the absence of disclosed revenue for the target. The wide peer range ($3.1B–$10.3B) reflects heterogeneous stage maturity and asset stage within Series C.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $260M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The substantial dispersion reflects tension between stage-progression mechanics on recent capital ($306M) and peer multiples anchored to late-stage biotech valuations. Key uncertainties include the target's clinical progress relative to peers, revenue-generating capacity, and the degree to which recent funding rounds reflect equity dilution versus valuation step-up. Peer heterogeneity—notably Colossal's outlier $10.3B—underscores the sensitivity of biotech valuation to differentiated clinical or commercial position.
